title: Zheng He
hookLine: the Muslim admiral of the Ming dynasty who sailed as far as East Africa

lines: A GIRAFFE AT THE EMPEROR'S COURT.
cards: A giraffe walks into the court of the emperor of China. Long neck, patterned coat, gentle eyes, swaying above officials in silk robes. Nobody at court quite knows what it is.

Some decide it must be a qilin, a creature of legend that appears only when the world is ruled well. The giraffe had come a very long way, from Africa, in the years when a great Chinese fleet was sailing those seas.
And the fleet's commander was a Muslim from the far southwest of China. Today: Zheng He.

teach.h: MA HE OF YUNNAN, FROM A MUSLIM FAMILY.
teach.b: Zheng He was born Ma He, in Yunnan, into a Muslim family. A stone inscription for his father calls him hajji, one who had made the pilgrimage to Mecca.

teach.h: CAPTURED, THEN TRUSTED BY AN EMPEROR.
teach.b: As a boy, Ma He was captured when the armies of the new Ming dynasty took Yunnan, and he was taken into the household of a prince. He rose, and became the prince's trusted servant.
When that prince became the Yongle emperor, the boy from Yunnan, now named Zheng He, became admiral of great fleets sent across the Indian Ocean.

teach.h: FLEETS FROM JAVA TO EAST AFRICA.
teach.b: They called at Java and Malacca, at Sri Lanka and the coast of India, at Hormuz in the Gulf, at ports of Arabia, and as far as the coast of East Africa.

They carried silk and porcelain, envoys and gifts, and sailed home with ambassadors, spices and gifts, among them, from envoys, giraffes. His Muslim interpreter, Ma Huan, wrote down what they saw in each land.

Zheng He sailed for an empire, not as a missionary; the voyages were about trade, power and prestige. But in ports from Java to Arabia he would have met Muslim communities who prayed as his family prayed.
The Qur'an says God has honored the children of Adam, and carries them on the land and the sea. In Java, temples and shrines still remember his name.
And here the journey through East and Southeast Asia ends: from traders on the straits to an admiral on the open ocean.

how: Zheng He is remembered in China as a great navigator, by Hui Muslims as one of their own, and in Southeast Asia at shrines and temples, such as Sam Po Kong in Semarang on Java, that bear his name.

games.q: you're at the emperor's court. an animal no one has seen walks in: long neck, patterned coat, gentle eyes. what do some of the officials decide it is?
o: a qilin, a creature of legend.
games.why: some took the giraffe for a qilin, a sign of a world ruled well.

practice: Choose a place far away that you'd love to reach someday, and trace the route in your mind: the first leg, the open stretch in the middle, the port where you'd rest. What would you carry, and what would you hope to bring back?
If you pray, you can ask for safe travel for everyone on the road today; if not, simply let the map open.
